subject: Dedicated capacity recommendation & hedging plan for Nebula (H100/A100/L4)
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@nebula.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nebula.ai, ops-team@nebula.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask – guidance on SKU mix for our mixed workload

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Nebula is moving from a pilot to a committed deployment and procurement wants a concrete SKU recommendation for Dedicated. High level on our workload:~

- Two main services: (1) long-context summarization (~8k token average, spikes to 32k for some docs) for our enterprise customers, and (2) high-throughput embedding + short chat used by internal tools (mostly 1–2k token requests, high QPS).
- Expected steady-state: ~150 qps of short requests, ~12 concurrent long-context sessions during business hours, with occasional batch spikes on month-end.
- Latency SLOs: 95th < 450ms for short chat; long-context < 3s for tail 95th.
- Security: data must stay in a dedicated VPC; some customers require KMS-backed keys.

Procurement would like a recommended Dedicated fleet mix between H100 / A100 / L4 (memory and perf tradeoffs), an ops hedging plan (what to do if long-context demand increases), and a ballpark for committed v. burst capacity. We have some internal usage traces attached (nebula-infer-profile.csv).

Can you send a short recommendation and we can sync on a follow-up demo?

—Marta
Lead Ops, Nebula Systems
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@nebula.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, procurement@nebula.ai
Date: 2026-12-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask – guidance on SKU mix for our mixed workload

Marta — thanks for the profile and clear constraints. High level recommendation below; attaching a short hedge runbook and cost workbook.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Reserve a mixed pool: H100-heavy for long-context, A100 for general purpose GPU throughput, and a small L4 pool for embedding/cheap chat burst. Rough starting split: H100 30%, A100 55%, L4 15% by reserved slot count.

Rationale (brief):
- Long-context: H100 (larger memory and better sparsity/FP16 throughput) handles 32k contexts with fewer tiling passes and better latency for tail loads. It reduces request fragmentation and KV-cache churn.
- High QPS short traffic: A100 remains cost-effective when scaled horizontally and is efficient for 1–2k token inference with good batching characteristics.
- Embeddings/cost-sensitive paths: L4 is substantially cheaper per token for smaller contexts and should be the primary target for embeddings and non-sensitive short completions.

Hedging & ops runbook (short):
- Commit baseline: reserve enough H100 slots for sustaining 12 concurrent long-context sessions with ~20% headroom (recommend compute to cover 14 active long sessions).
- Burst pool: configure autoscale to spill long-context overflow to ephemeral H100 instances (if available) and to A100 with a graceful degradation policy (downsample context length or fall back to segmented summarization).
- L4 fallback: route low-sensitivity embeddings and short chats to L4 by default; promote to A100 only on auth/feature flags.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for long-context sessions; this can reduce H100 reserve needs by ~15–25% depending on overlap.

Operational knobs & tradeoffs:
- Memory-bound models will favor H100: if your long-context model is memory-heavy (large weights + huge KV), you'll see lower tail latency on H100. If the long model is more compute-bound after quantization, A100 is more competitive.
- If Nebula wants to minimize committed spend, increase L4 share but accept higher latencies/segmented outputs for long docs.

Next steps I propose:
1) We run a 48–72h pilot on Dedicated with a 30/55/15 slot mix using your trace to validate tail latencies and token costs.
2) We instrument KV cache and sim some overlap scenarios; tweak reserve sizes.
3) Post-pilot: agree a commit level (monthly GPU-hours) and burst policy.

Attachments: sku-cost-projections-DEAL-5893.xlsx (cost by slot & token), hedge-runbook-v1.md (ops checklist).

If that looks sensible I can loop in procurement and ops for a 30-minute alignment next week.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: internal: pricing impact for DEAL-5893

Naomi / Irene — quick internal note on pricing and commits:

- If Nebula commits to a 12-month reserved spend that covers the baseline reserve (H100x14, A100 equivalent, L4 pool), we can offer a blended discount of 12% on token price and preferential burst prioritization.
- If they prefer quarterly commits, suggest a 6% discount but require a higher buffer in reserved slots (add ~10% headroom) to manage operational risk.

Key commercial ask: confirm whether procurement needs a hard cap on month-to-month billing or is comfortable with a committed-minimum + variable burst billing. The latter preserves flexibility to grow without renegotiation.

Also: include a clause that allows temporary cross-region failover to our secondary US region during extreme spikes (>X% occupied) — that reduces the need for large reserve on-prem.

—Ben
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@nebula.ai>
Date: 2026-12-04T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask – guidance on SKU mix for our mixed workload

Looping ops concerns into the thread for Marta's visibility. High level ops constraints and mitigations:

- Autoscaling / cold-starts: H100 cold-starts for large KV caches can add 700–1200ms; we recommend warm standby slots (a tiny fraction of H100 reserve) to keep cold-start probability <5%.
- Monitoring: we will provision token-level cost tracing and per-slot tail latency dashboards; set alerts on KV miss rate and eviction rate.
- Fallback policy (simple):
  1) If H100 queue > 85% for 5m, prioritize active customer sessions and reject non-critical batch jobs.
  2) If queue remains >90% for 10m, reroute new long-context sessions to A100 with a warning banner and algorithmic segmentation.
- Quantization: if Nebula can accept bf16->int8 quantized variant for parts of the model, A100 performance gap narrows and you can shift ~10–15% of long-workload to A100. That should be a measurable config change during the pilot.

I'll prepare a short ops playbook for the pilot that lists metrics, runbook steps, and SLA degradation banners.

Irene
Director, Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask – guidance on SKU mix for our mixed workload — proposed pilot and timeline

Marta / team — consolidating and proposing next steps so we have a single plan to share with procurement: 

Proposal snapshot:
- Pilot (48–72h): reserve H100x14 slots, A100 slots sized to support 150 qps short traffic with batching (~A100 equivalent of 40 slots), L4 pool of 8 slots.
- Instrumentation: KV cache enabled, token-level tracing, alerts for KV miss > 20% and H100 tail > 3s.
- Commercial: 6-month pilot credit covering burst H100 hours; if post-pilot Nebula chooses 12-month commit at the proposed reserve, Redwood offers 12% blended discount and a prioritized burst queue.

Deliverables & owners:
- Redwood: run pilot, share latency/cost report and ops playbook (Irene) — target report by 2026-12-12.
- Nebula: confirm sample dataset and approve KMS/VPC config by 2026-12-09 (Marta + procurement).
- Joint: 30m post-pilot review on 2026-12-13 (calendar invite linked).

If that timeline works I'll send the formal SOW and the pilot onboarding checklist. Meeting link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/meet/naomi/nebula-kickoff-2026-12-10

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Naomi
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
